text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) urges dialogue between Serbian opposition and the authorities during talks in Copenhagen with opposition coalition Zajedno leaders Vesna Pesic and Vuk Draskovic.

- French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette called on Yugoslavia to postpone ratification of its special ties agreement with the Bosnian Serbs until the High Representative to Bosnia Carl Bildt gives his approval.

- International Mediator in former Yugoslavia succession talks Sir Arthur Watts says the sharing of assets of the former Yugoslavia is a complicated process and will require a long time. He is now visiting Macedonia and Slovenia and will visit Sarajevo, Zagreb and Belgrade in April.
- Serbian parliament adopts agreement on special parallel ties between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb Republic.

- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic says his statements during his Washington visit were in line with realisation of national interest of Montenegro and strengthening of Yugoslavia as a joint state.
- Deputies of Montenegro's opposition coalition National Accord walked out of the republic's parliament session because of pressure put on opposition leaders including a libel trial against them.
- Serbia to issue a tender for allocation of available radio and TV frequencies in April.

- Serbian arms factories workers will protest in front of the federal parliament on Wednesday because the government has not met their demands to resolve the arms factory status and pay outstanding debts of $165 million and 42 million dinars.
- Clothing factory Jumko from Vranje advertises 1,000 job openings and may advertise for more later in the year said general manager of the company Voja Dimic.

- Yugoslav delegation for succession of the former Yugoslavia met with representatives of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) in Basle in March and revoked agreement for the $200 million assets to be divided outside the succession package. - Southern Serbian town of Nis is a recruitment centre for Serbian mercenaries sent to Zaire writes a Nis daily.
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives Serbian government on its three-year anniversary stresses importance of realisation of planned reforms which include ownership and structural changes.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic ends visit to France says the two sides agreed to continue dialogue.
- Montenegrin Prime Minister continues to undermine Yugoslavia and Serbia despite his claims to the contrary, commentary which includes Djukanovic's letters to U.S. congressmen.
- Serbian Opposition leader Vuk Draskovic visiting Bonn on Tuesday.
- Kraljevo wagons factory concluds $11 million deal for exporting 402 freight wagons to Myanmar by February 1988.
- Carpet factory Sintelon from Backa Palanka plans to export to the value of 57 million German marks in 1997.
- The new Serbian draft privatisation law will be presented to the public in the course of this week.
BORBA
- President of Yugoslav Chambger of Commerce says Yugoslavia is open for cooperation invites foreign partners to invest in the country at gathering in Salonica.
- Opposition continues purge of public firms in Kragujevac, 200 people have been replaced so far.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Traders at Belgrade's main flea market say unless city authorities find a way to regulate their status by March 24, they will throw out the market's management and form a kind of "public enterprise" of their own.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Belgrade traders say people bying food less than during the time of hyperinflation (1993). Most people just buy bread and milk.
